topic: what the phone's main thread waits on; compute per tick and a real clock in the speed harness
observation: 4e removed 3.6 points of main-thread samples but ticks per second rose ~1%, and main-thread samples per tick did not fall (31.05 -> 31.0). The phone profile samples cycles at 1000 Hz; the main thread gave ~617 samples per second, i.e. on the CPU ~62% of the time.
schedstat: per-thread /proc/<pid>/task/*/schedstat over 10 s windows during the 4f run1 (scratchpad phone_schedstat.sh): loading 91-100% on-CPU; gameplay main thread ~62% on-CPU, ~0.4% run-queue wait, ~37% off-CPU with ~105 context switches per second; render workers ~20% each
offcpu: simpleperf --trace-offcpu -e cpu-clock (android_speed.py --offcpu, rt-speed/rt4f-offcpu-profile): main thread 20.28 s recorded, 7.56 s (37%) off-CPU, 99.8% of it in __epoll_pwait <- android::Looper::pollOnce <- MessageQueue.nativePollOnce; 1,785 waits in ~20 s, 1,316 of them 4-6 ms (6.87 s, median 5.14 ms)
cause: OriginalRuntimeSession schedules the next iteration after the sum of the game's Sleep calls (asyncAfter). The original timer (OriginalApplicationTimer, EXE 43d157..43d1ef) dispatches a tick when more than 33 ms passed since its baseline and otherwise sleeps min(remainder, 5) ms. android_speed.py ran with --virtual-clock 123456789 8 (8 ms per message-loop iteration), so every tick takes ~4 iterations and the 3 idle ones sleep 5 ms for real: ~16 ms of every tick is pacing whatever the compute time.
harness: android_speed.py: --offcpu (off-CPU call graphs), --real-clock (no virtual clock), and per-thread compute per tick (mainCpuShare/renderCpuShare from schedstat between bodies 600 and 1500; mainMsPerTick/renderMsPerTick = share x 1000 / ticks per second)
result: 4f: virtual clock main 30.4 ms, render 22.2 ms per tick at 20.43 ticks per second; real clock 30.25 ticks per second (the game's own rate is at most 30.3), main 26.1 ms, render 19.3 ms. Tier 1 (33 ms compute per tick on each thread) is met; an idle message-loop iteration costs ~1.6 ms of main-thread CPU ((30.4-26.1) ms over ~2.6 fewer idle iterations per tick).
